recipes.name: Caramel Snack Mix
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) package crispy corn and rice cereal

steps.text: Preheat oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Spray a large roasting pan with non-stick cooking spray.
In a medium-size microwave safe bowl, mix butter, white corn syrup and brown sugar. Place the mixture in the microwave and cook 2 minutes, or until butter melts.
Place the cereal, pecans and almonds into the prepared roasting pan. Pour the melted butter mixture over the cereal and nuts and mix gently until the cereal and nuts are coated.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
As the snack mix is cooling, be sure to continue to stir so that the mix will not harden in one big lump.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Snack Mix
raw_recipe.description: Blend butter with cereal and toasted nuts to make this sweet cocktail munchie that disappears by the handful.

review.reviewBody: Great snack mix! I also found it a bit sweet the first time I made it, so the next time I used salted nuts (pecans, cashews and almonds) and also added some pretzels. It was a big hit with my family!

I always add unsalted, dry-roasted peanuts to this mix and bake it in a huge turkey roasting pan. When I lay it out for cooling, I use parchment paper, and spread it out as far as possible in a thin layer so I don't end up with huge clumps. Then I put about a cup & a half in sandwich sized ziploc bags for storage, or for giving out. My family absolutely LOVES this recipe. It is the best Chex Mix recipe we have ever tried, far superior to any other.

Love this snack mix and make it every year about this time. Package it and give most of it away, but always keep some for myself too!
I use organic multi-grain cereal, increase the quantity of both pecans and almonds (and chop the almonds)to about 3 cups total. When I take it out of the oven I dump it onto parchment paper and spread it out and let it cool for about 3 hours. No problems with stickiness or a big lump of mix and I don't have to keep stirring either!

So easy and a big hit with everyone! I've made it twice now with great success and little cleanup. I lined two half sheet pans with foil and sprayed them with butter flavored non-stick spray. I added a handful of pretzel snaps and used pecan halves.

Melt the butter, sugar and syrup in the microwave until the butter is melted and the sugar is dissolved. Stir it well. This took more than 2 minutes in my microwave, it took about 4. This is not a cooking stage, the mixture will caramelize from its time in the oven. Stir every 15 minutes with a silicone spatula, gently stirring and turning the cereal and nuts so they all get some coating. 

After the hour, I poured it all out on my kitchen counter which I lined with parchment paper. Here I stirred until cool, again gently. After a few minutes you can put your hands into it and spread it out/stir some more.

After it's completely cool, put it in an air tight container. Looks pretty in cellophane gift bags with a pretty ribbon. 

Thanks for the recipe, this is a keeper!

I will definitely make this again and again! Both times I have made this, I have changed it up slightly but it is still amazing! The first time I followed the recipe exactly but added a few pinches of sea salt to the caramel mixture and it was so good. The second time I made it I cut back on the brown sugar to 3/4 cup, added a few pinches of sea salt to the Carmel mixture. I also added a few handfuls of pretzel sticks and about a cup of peanuts to the cereal mixture and had more than enough of the caramel mix to coat it all. The most important key to this recipe is the constant stirring as it cools to avoid sticking together and stickiness after it cools. My new favorite go to snack mix, my family and friends love it too!

I use LIFE cereal, salted almonds and pecans pieces which makes this treat totally addictive! Be sure to stir the mixture in the oven every 15 minutes during baking and most critical is to stir it frequently once you take it out of the oven. If you don't stir it repeatedly after you have baked it for an hour, you will get hardened lumps. By stirring the mixture while it's still warm it will be coated evenly and will be lump free. This recipe is so addictive that my friends and family have dubbed it candy crack. ??

I have this exact recipe but it is made from start to finish in the microwave. Mine says to cook the butter,syrup,and brown sugar for 2 min. in the microwave and stir. Then cook 2 min. more. Put the cereal into a large microwavable bowl and pour syrup mixture over to coat,stirring gently. Microwave an additional 4 min. stirring every minute. Pour on parchment paper to cool and break apart. I add peanuts,pretzels and choc. covered candies when cool. Love this recipe!

wow, easy to see why this is so addictive! The versatility of this simple recipe is amazing, as the possibilities are endless. I used half corn chex, and half peanut butter chex. all peanuts, some leftover dried cranberries, and mini pretzels. Out of habit, I did the syrup on the stove in a sauce pan, and did add 1/2 tsp salt and some vanilla to the syrup. After it came out of the oven, I poured it onto a large cookie sheet to cool. I didn't have to break up much at all. It is buttery, toffee goodness that would make a great party mix, or to give away as gifts. The problem comes with being able to stop eating it! such a great recipe that allows you to be creative, and the ratio of syrup to cereal/nuts is spot on. thanks so much. sure to be a crowd-pleaser, and will make again and again.

This was amazingly easy and very, very good! I used chopped pecans, cashews and pretzel sticks. (Next time, will use pecan halves.) Added 2 caps full of vanilla extract and about 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon to the mixture after the butter melted. Will add one full teaspoon of cinnamon next time because I could not taste it. When it came out of the oven, I placed the pan on the counter, under the ceiling fan and stirred constantly for the first 10 minutes of cooling time. It is a day later and what looked like a MASSIVE amount of mix has been reduced to about one cup. Guess I'd better make more.

This mix is awesomely delicious. I haven't taken it yet to it's destination but I hope I don't make myself sick eating it before I get it there! I needed to double the recipe. When I got it all mixed with the cereal and nuts it seemed like it was still awfully gooey so I added more dry ingredients and still had plenty to cover the mix. I used 14 oz of corn chex, 17 oz cinnamon crunch, about 3/4 lb pretzel twists, 2 c. pecans and 1 1/2 c whole almonds. Once I'd baked it I turned it out onto rimmed cookie sheets so that it would be in a single layer and then tossed it as it cooled with two spatulas, like tossing a salad. It cooled nicely and didn't glob up. I suspect if you use the ratio with more sugar/butter mix to the dry ingredients it would have more of a tendency to stick together and be more candy-like. However, mine turned out plenty caramel-ly! It's a little labor intensive since you have to turn it every 15 minutes then toss while cooling and I made a sticky mess of several pans and utensils, but it's worth it! Definitely a keeper and I can see how, if you take this to a group, you'll be commanded to keep bringing it!

Great recipe! I made this exactly as stated in the recipe, using Chex Multigrain cereal, almonds and pecans. I left the nuts whole, and toasted them in the oven first. I saw several 'bad' reviews, and I believe most of them complained about stickiness of the finished product. These same reviewers stated that they 'had' to increase the cook time for the coating in the microwave to get it to the hard crack stage. That's their mistake right there! Like the recipe says, you just put it in the microwave until the butter melts! Stir it and pour it over your cereal mixture. I couldn't find my roaster so I used 2-9x13 cake pans, then dumped it on sheets of quick release foil and spread it out. It took almost no time to cool and didn't have to be stirred. Next time I'm going to try adding some cinnamon and vanilla as others suggested. Great recipe, Trish!
I made 4x the recipe. And my Church family will taste it tomorrow. I'll let ya know
It was super good and I'm going to sell it at a school market next week. (it turned out great!)
This is a delicious recipe! I added two cups of deluxe mixed nuts instead of the pecans and almonds alone.
Big fan! Yum. I like salty with sweet so used salted cashews and pretzels but its the caramel that makes this one. Very nice.
Everyone loves this it is so good. Very easy to make. This is one of my favorites.

I made a couple of slight changes. I made a double batch and used 1/4 plain cheerios with 3/4 Crispex. I used the pecans but left out the almonds. Everything else was as directed. I made it for a church worker meeting. Everyone kept helping themselves to more and more...and more (I had plenty)! My pastor called me the next day asking if I could make another batch just for him.?? It was the perfect mid-afternoon pick-me-up snack.
Really really good. I added the dried cranberries after it cooked like someone else had done. This is a keeper

This was an easy dish to make and very tasty. If you are counting calories, DO NOT MAKE THIS!. It is almost impossible to resist, so you just keep eating and eating. Perfect combo of salty sweet. Definite cheat on your calorie count for the day.
